correctness.rationale: A proper border of any six-run alternating word has 2 or 4 runs; a 4-run border forces a 2-run border. A run-boundary rotation is therefore unbordered iff its first run exceeds the penultimate run or its second run is shorter than the final run. The six comparisons list all possible unbordered rotations; interior cuts have a length-one border. Each of the 13 weak-order types for each of two triples has a proven exact rational weight; summing the 169 products yields the displayed spectrum by verifiable finite integer-polynomial identities. Direct border enumeration of 4096 sextuples and independent fixed-length counts to 18 pass. Pole analysis rigorously proves the 4/5 limit; finite tests are not substituted for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus semantic queries, accessible existing-claim deduplication, targeted literature searches, primary-text examination of Clokie et al. 2019 and Holub–Müller 2015/2016, and database comparisons revealed no equivalent six-run inequality law or length-spectrum enumeration. The unrestricted global results and exact-two classification do not entail the conditional six-run rational functions. The 2004 Harju–Nowotka full text was not available and leaves a material unindexed-specialization risk. Search failure alone is not treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Cyclic borders and unbordered conjugates are established natural invariants. For the first natural six-run family, the result determines every unbordered cut with a six-comparison formula, all possible counts and all length-by-count enumerators, the sharp maximum of five first possible at length 11, and the conditional limiting distribution split equally between 4 and 5. These are complete structural and enumerative assertions, not a table increment, renaming or a routine general theorem corollary.
